newsitem.title: UK: Mideast/Japan crude tanker rates set to stay firm.
newsitem.headline: Mideast/Japan crude tanker rates set to stay firm.

text.p: Chartering rates for very large crude carriers (VLCCs) moving to Japan from the Mideast are likely to stay firm after a rise this week to W67.5 and above, ship brokers said.
"The driving force in tanker markets at the moment is for VLCCs going east out of the AG," one said.

Hyundai's fixture of the 260,000 tonne Taos to Korea at W67.5 and Kyushu's W85 paid for the 250,000 tonne Diamond City to Japan were seen as representing the market, although slightly lower than the W72.5 paid earlier in the week.
"There is a lack of tonnage and these rates are going to stay up here well into June and probably into July," a broker said.
Ssangyong's fixture of the 270,000 tonne Sovereign Unity to Korea was seen slightly below the market because it is an old ship.
"All the other markets are basically flat," the broker said.
Markets for VLCCs from West Africa across the North Atlantic were seen steady at W65, while Suezmaxes were seen flat at W95.
North Sea markets were also steady with a number of 80,000 tonners fixed at around W135-W140, and no enquiry was heard for transatlantic voyages fom this region.
